properties.title: Port Sudan: night lights 45% below its recent nights (NASA Black Marble, 27 Nov 2026)
properties.summary: NASA's Black Marble (near real time, NOAA-20) gives 0.76 nW/cm²/sr over a box about 44 km across Port Sudan on the night of 27 Nov 2026, 45% below the median of the 10 clear nights in the 14 before it (1.39). 80% of the box was clear, so part of the city went unmeasured that night. A drop in light fits a grid failure, strikes on the grid, rationing or load shedding, and also smoke, dust or snow the cloud mask missed; Blackout measures how much darker it was, not why. NASA advises against using near-real-time data for tactical decisions or local-scale conditions.

baseline_ref.window: median of the counted nights (at least 60% of the box clear) in the 14 nights before, at least 5 of them (BO-IND-15)

sources.publisher: NASA (Black Marble, VIIRS on NOAA-20; near real time from NASA LANCE, standard from LAADS DAAC)
sources.title: VJ146A2 Gap-Filled Lunar BRDF-Adjusted Nighttime Lights Daily
sources.licence: NASA Earth science data: no restrictions on use, citation requested (Black Marble VJ146A2, DOI 10.5067/VIIRS/VJ146A2.002, and its near-real-time version from NASA LANCE); near-real-time data are provided as is under the LANCE disclaimer
sources.descriptor: Night radiance with moonlight and surface effects removed, about 500 m pixels, one pass a night. Blackout averages the clear pixels in a box about 44 km across each watched city.

sources.descriptor: Cloudflare's automated detection on RouteViews, RIPE RIS and its own route collectors: origin hijacks with Cloudflare's confidence score and evidence, and provider-customer-provider leaks. It says what the collectors saw, not who meant it.
sources.title: Cloudflare Radar BGP hijack and route-leak detection

properties.summary: Cloudflare Radar's route-leak detection lists 2 provider-customer-provider leaks by this network since 2026-11-24T21:39:14Z, all finished; the largest carried 145 prefixes from 1 origin networks and was seen by 43 of Radar's 280 route-collector peers. Paths (upstream > leaker > customer): AS1299 (Arelion Sweden AB) > AS4775 > AS1273; AS6453 (TATA COMMUNICATIONS (AMERICA) INC) > AS4775 > AS1273. Event IDs: 680650, 680649. A leak can send traffic the long way round or drop it; most are export mistakes (BO-H-4B). Reported by Cloudflare; Blackout does not assess intent.
